Cached-id resolution calls session.identityProviders().getById(id), re-entering the caching provider, instead of idpDelegate.getById(id).

Test testCacheIDPForLogin (not in methods_read) registers cleanup for identityProviders().get("alias") instead of "idp-alias-" + i, so the created IdPs are not removed (same mistake again at line 425 for idp-alias-20).
getBouncyCastleProvider returns the provider of the default KeyStore type rather than a BouncyCastle provider.
Lines 114-115 create ASN1Encoder instances and write r and s, then discard them; the return statement re-encodes with fresh encoders (dead code inside the anonymous ECDSACryptoProvider).

readSequence does `length = length - bytes.length` on the value from readLength, which returns -1 for indefinite-length encoding (line 134); the -1 is never handled, so such sequences are silently read as empty.
New abstract `int order()` on the public CryptoProvider interface (no default) breaks every existing third-party implementation.

Feature-disabled branch calls picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED), which calls System.exit directly; the identical new call is in UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run line 48 (ambiguous which file the comment meant).

Constant declaration (not a method; covered only by the CompatibilityResult.java::<top-level> entry): RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changes 4 to 3 and 4 becomes FEATURE_DISABLED with no release note or migration guidance; this is a missing-docs comment, so the location is the changed constant.
Removal-event cleanup is gated on Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) instead of ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2, so with only V2 enabled permissions are orphaned.

findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()) uses the server id as owner, but getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with owner resourceServer.getClientId() (line 104), so per-client resources are never found.

findByType(CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) only yields the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type), and line 140 returns its name rather than client ids, which callers pass to realm.getClientById.
getResourceTypeResource (line 217) can return null and the result is passed to findByResource and later resource.getScopes() without a null check.
Private getEvaluationContext (with its anonymous getBaseAttributes override) is never called.
canManage() falls back to hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), so a VIEW-only grant passes the manage check; it should check MANAGE only.
Passes and collects groupResource.getId() (resource id) although hasPermission resolves resources by name (the group id) and callers expect group ids, so per-group grants do not yield the right ids.
